kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Considering the trees in question palms, from the Sauraseni Prakrit predecessor of Hindi ताड़ी (tāṛī, “palm-sap, toddy”), and based on a relation to pines via Aramaic – encountered as Jewish Palestinian Aramaic דדינין, דדנין (daddīnīn, plural), Classical Syriac ܕܐܕܝܢ (/⁠dāḏīn⁠/) – from Ancient Greek δᾳδίον (dāidíon, “resinous pine wood, Kien”), diminutive of δαΐς (daḯs, “pinewood”).
s: Ancient Greek δᾳδίον (dāidíon, “resinous pine wood, Kien”)
g: sap or resin of a tree
St. John's wort (Hypericum gen. et spp.)
